- introduced a safer public API, `kthSmallest(int[] values, int k)`, with explicit validation for `null`, empty arrays, and out-of-range `k` values at [quickselect.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/041_quickselect/quickselect.java:30)
- replaced the recursive selection flow with an iterative core at [quickselect.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/041_quickselect/quickselect.java:35), which is easier to reason about and avoids unnecessary recursion
- extracted duplicated swap logic into a helper and tightened the partition loop at [quickselect.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/041_quickselect/quickselect.java:9)
- simplified the demo entry point at [quickselect.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/041_quickselect/quickselect.java:71) so it uses the new API directly

Verified with `javac quickselect.java` and `java QuickSelect`; the program prints `K-th smallest element in array: 6`.

One remaining algorithmic limitation is that pivot selection is still deterministic (`values[high]`), so worst-case input can still degrade to `O(n^2)`. If you want, I can do a second pass to randomize the pivot and add a small test harness.
